html:
SMTO-PRL-0009 — A step was interrupted and wasn't run again

GUID: 971b0115-0509-49b2-b8ff-1e6ecf038772
Slug: activity-recovery-interrupted
Domain: PRL · Subsystem: prl

What happened

  • SMTO was interrupted, for example by a restart, while steps were running. Steps that had started may or may not have finished; steps that hadn't started were cancelled. SMTO didn't rerun anything by itself.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Activities section under this task. Steps marked unknown (with a ? mark) had started; steps marked cancelled never ran. This shows which steps need checking and which simply didn't happen.
  2. For each unknown step, check the place it would have changed, such as a file, a service or a computer, to see whether the change is there. A step that started may have finished its work before the interruption.
  3. Send a message telling SMTO which steps finished, and ask it to continue only with what's left. SMTO can then finish the work without repeating a change that already happened.

What success looks like

  • SMTO continues with the remaining steps, and the Activities section shows them completing.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask SMTO to rerun every step from the start; some may already have made their changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Batch recovery found no trustworthy result for an interrupted activity: running or claimed work was marked outcome_unknown and unstarted work was cancelled with executed:false; nothing was replayed.

What this means

  • Recovery cannot find a trustworthy result for an interrupted activity; running/claimed work becomes outcome_unknown while unstarted work may become cancelled with executed:false. Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.

Why this can happen

  • Recovery cannot find a trustworthy result for an interrupted activity; running/claimed work becomes outcome_unknown while unstarted work may become cancelled with executed:false.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect invocation evidence and prior activity state to distinguish unknown effects from confirmed unstarted cancellation.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the run's activity receipts and the current external state for each outcome_unknown activity, then continue only the work still needed; cancelled activities with executed:false did not run. Recovery never replays an unknown operation.
  • Inspect existing activity receipts and current external state, then continue only remaining eligible work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing effects are reconciled and only eligible remaining work continues.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Activity ownership, preflight and durable receipts determine admission and effect certainty. Rejected new work does not erase prior child effects; recovery and diagnostics never replay an unknown operation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
